sections.body:
This is a story about a girl called Mai. She lives near the sea. She has watched boats all her life and eaten fish every week. But she has never been under the water.

On her birthday, her uncle takes her out in a small boat. There is a diving suit waiting for her, and a mask with a soft rubber edge.

A good adventure has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who is going and why. The middle brings the surprise. The end gives you something worth keeping.

This adventure has that shape. At the beginning, Mai is cold and a bit afraid in the boat. In the middle, the water goes from green to blue to a colour that has no name. At the end, she meets something that has been waiting a very long time to meet her.

Read it slowly. Feel the water get colder. Then tell the story to someone you trust.
examples: This story is about a girl who dives under the sea.
A good adventure has a beginning, a middle and an end.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this sea adventure is about

sections.body:
The boat smells of salt and diesel. It rocks a little, and the sky is enormous above it.

Mai's uncle shows her the gear. First the **mask**, with a soft rubber edge that seals around her eyes so the water cannot get in. Then the **fins** for her feet, which are long and flat and make her legs feel like new things. Then the **air tank** on her back, and the mouthpiece that hangs in front of her chest.

She puts the mask up. Everything goes green and wavery, like looking through a bowl of water.

She is scared. Not of the water exactly. Of the idea of her head going under it.

Her uncle says the one thing that helps: breathe out slowly, and the water will not go in.

Mai steps off the boat. The sea closes over her head.

The first thing she notices is the sound. Under the water there is no wind, no boat, no talking. There is only her own breathing, bubbling up past her ears. It sounds like a small animal that lives with her.
examples: The boat smelled of salt and diesel.
The mask had a soft rubber edge around her eyes.
The only sound was her own breathing, bubbling past her ears.
sections.heading: The beginning: cold feet on a warm boat

sections.body:
Mai kicks with her fins. She goes down.

The first colour is green. Green light from the sun comes down and turns everything the colour of a swimming pool. Small silver fish swim above her head, quick as sparks.

Then the green goes away. The blue comes in, and the blue is deeper. It is not the blue of a painted wall. It is the blue of the inside of the sky at night.

Then the light changes again. There is a colour that has no name in any language Mai knows. It is a dark blue-green that seems to glow by itself.

She looks up. Above her, the surface is a shining silver lid. The sun makes a coin of light that moves as she moves.

The air from her tank feels strange down here. It is cold and dry, and it tastes like yesterday. Her ears feel funny, so she stops and holds still until the funny feeling goes away.

Then she sees the reef.

It comes up out of the dark like a city made of coloured stone. Corals branch and wave. Fan shapes open and close. And everywhere, small bright fish move in and out like people going home.
examples: The first colour was green, like a swimming pool.
The surface was a shining silver lid above her.
The reef came out of the dark like a city of coloured stone.
sections.heading: The middle: the colours of the deep

sections.body:
Mai swims slowly along the reef. She keeps her hands close to her body, because she has been told not to touch.

The coral is alive. It is not stone. It is a colony of tiny animals, each one building a little wall for the reef. If you touch it, it can break, and it can take many years to grow back.

Then something moves past her. Slowly. Something big.

It is a **sea turtle**. Her shell is brown and green and shaped like an old plate. Her front flippers move as if she is swimming through air.

Mai's heart beats hard. She has seen turtle pictures in books. She has never seen one move.

The turtle swims past her. Then she stops. Then she turns around.

She swims back towards Mai. Right up to her. Close enough that Mai can see the small round eye looking at her through the mask.

And the turtle says something. Not in words. In a low soft sound, like a cat far away. But Mai understands it perfectly.

"Hello," the turtle says. "I have been waiting for you."

Nobody had told Mai that anything down here could talk. Nobody had told her that she would be understood.

Then the turtle turns and swims up, towards the silver lid of the surface, and Mai follows. All the way up, until the water breaks and the air hits her face and the boat is there again.
examples: The turtle's flippers moved as if she were swimming through air.
The turtle turned around and came back to her.
The water broke and the boat was there again.
sections.heading: The surprise: the turtle that knew her name

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **diving mask** covers your eyes and has glass in it. It lets you see under the water clearly.

Fins are flat rubber shoes for your feet. They push the water behind you so you go faster with less effort.

An **air tank** is a bottle of compressed air that a diver carries on their back. You breathe through a mouthpiece from this tank.

Coral is a hard, colourful structure built by tiny animals. It looks like a plant, but it is made of living creatures. Never touch it.

A **reef** is a whole underwater city of coral. Reefs are home to thousands of kinds of fish.
examples: A diving mask lets you see under the water.
Coral is alive, so we do not touch it.
sections.heading: The words inside this story

terms.example: She pulled the diving mask down over her nose.
terms.gloss: A cover for your eyes with glass in it. It lets you see under the water clearly.

terms.example: Her fins made a soft whirr in the water.
terms.gloss: Flat rubber shoes for your feet. They push the water behind you so you swim faster.

terms.example: Her uncle checked the air tank before she jumped in.
terms.gloss: A bottle of compressed air that a diver carries on their back and breathes from.

terms.example: The orange coral stood up like a tree.
terms.gloss: A hard, colourful structure built by tiny animals. It looks like a plant but it is alive, so never touch it.

terms.example: The reef was busy with small bright fish.
terms.gloss: A whole underwater city of coral. Thousands of kinds of fish live there.

sections.body:
What did Mai learn? She learned that the sea is not one thing. It has floors and colours and cities. It has a green shallows and a blue middle and a place where the light makes its own colour.

She learned something else too. She was afraid of the water under her head, and she went in anyway. The fear did not go away first. She just took the step while it was still there.

And she learned to be careful with what is not hers. The coral belongs to the reef, and the reef belongs to the fish.

Here is how to tell this adventure to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with who is going and why. Tell the hard part in the middle. Save the surprise for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this adventure is this: go and see the big thing. It may be waiting for you.
examples: The story starts with a girl in a boat on her birthday.
The surprise comes at the very end.
Go and see the big thing, because it may be waiting for you.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start with the character: Mai in the boat on her birthday, a little afraid.
Tell the middle: the green water, the blue dark and the coral reef below.
Tell the surprise: the sea turtle that turns around and comes back.
End with the lesson: go and see the big thing, it may be waiting for you.

item.summary: A girl puts on her diving mask and swims down to the coral reef for the very first time. Follow her through the shallow water, the dark blue middle and the reef at the bottom. After reading, you can retell the adventure, use five new sea words in your own sentences, and explain why you should never touch a living coral.
item.title: My First Adventure Under the Sea
